title: A tested CFPB narrative filter does not expose the consumer meaning or outcome stages
source_unit: Live CFPB public complaint API query and same-query control for credit-card complaints carrying a monetary-relief response label
geography: United States complaint records; API query received dates 2025-01-01 through 2026-09-18

observations.period: Control query; credit card; closed with monetary relief; 2025-01-01 through 2026-09-18

narrative_field_present.unit: usable narrative fields in returned response payload

observed_response_fields.unit: administrative fields exposed in returned payload

observations.method: Live official CFPB API control query with field=all and size=25; raw response was hashed but not retained.
observations.uncertainty: A response-shape result is specific to the tested endpoint, filters, vintage, and access tier; it is not evidence that consumers lacked narratives.
observations.subgroup: Credit-card complaints with company_response=Closed with monetary relief.
observations.counterinterpretation: Narrative text may exist in another endpoint, vintage, or administrative system; the absence here is an API observability boundary, not a consumer-level zero.

observations.period: Probe query; same filters plus has_narrative=true; 2025-01-01 through 2026-09-18

returned_ids_identical_to_control.unit: boolean comparison of returned complaint IDs

narrative_field_present.unit: usable narrative fields in returned response payload

observations.method: Live official CFPB API probe using the control query plus has_narrative=true; raw response was hashed but not retained.
observations.uncertainty: Identical IDs and totals show only what this tested parameter did in this response shape; they do not establish that the filter is semantically implemented across all routes.
observations.subgroup: Same credit-card and company-response query with the narrative filter added.
observations.counterinterpretation: The filter may be ignored, response fields may be suppressed, or narratives may be unavailable to this public route; all remain distinct explanations.

denominator.unit: paired live API queries with identical base filters

returned_id_set_difference.unit: IDs differing between probe and control

meaning_or_alternative_stage.unit: usable fields exposed for narrative meaning or alternative/non-use decision

observations.method: Paired query comparison using retained aggregate diagnostics, field inventories, and response hashes.
observations.uncertainty: The pair rules out only the tested shortcut; it does not measure complaint incidence, narrative prevalence, remedy receipt, account correction, trust, switching, or exit.
observations.subgroup: One narrow public-API route and its control.
observations.counterinterpretation: A stable administrative response label can coexist with unobserved customer experience; `Closed with monetary relief` remains a company-reported category, not verified relief receipt.

related_sources.claim: Reproduction record containing query parameters, field inventory, response hashes, and bounded interpretation.

boundary: This is a public-API schema and filter boundary. It does not establish narrative absence among consumers, complaint incidence, verified monetary relief or receipt, account correction, repeat effort, trust, switching, or exit. The next qualifying route requires lawful linked, consented, or account-level follow-up with those stages.
